# SigComply CLI

> SigComply runs in your GitHub Actions or GitLab CI pipeline, checks cloud and SaaS configuration against SOC 2 and ISO 27001, and signs the evidence into storage you own; it is for teams that won't give a compliance vendor access to their cloud, code host or identity provider, and for startups preparing a first audit that want a pipeline step rather than a platform rollout. The `sigcomply` CLI pulls configuration from AWS, GCP, Azure, GitHub, GitLab, Okta and Active Directory with read-only credentials and evaluates it against SOC 2 and ISO 27001 policies whose source anyone can read. For controls no API can answer, it checks that uploaded documents are present for the period, merges them into one PDF to validate them, signs a record of the files' hashes, and stores the merged PDF in the customer's vault; it never judges document content. Evidence stays in storage the customer owns. With SigComply Cloud (paid, with a 2-month free trial) it also sends per-policy counts, never identities, to a dashboard. It does not make anyone compliant.

Facts agents get wrong:

- The config key is singular: `framework: soc2` or `framework: iso27001`. No other framework exists.
- `sigcomply check` reads the framework from `.sigcomply.yaml` and has no `--framework` flag.
- Exit codes: `0` no failures; `1` a policy failed or declared scope is incomplete (the default; `ci.fail_on_violation: false` turns it off); `2` execution error, including a policy with status `error` and unknown or conflicting flags; `3` configuration error.
- Cloud submission happens only when `cloud.base_url` (for example `https://sigcomply.com`) or `--cloud-url` is set, and the run is in CI with an OIDC token. `cloud.project_id` names the dashboard project (`prj_` followed by 20 base58 characters (letters and digits except 0, O, I and l), copied from the project's page; never invent one); without it a run that submits exits 3 before collecting. Only full runs submit (`sigcomply check` with no filter, or `--scheduled`); `--cadence`, `--cadences`, `--on-push` and `--pr` runs never do.
- Binding slot names: `evidence` for most policies, `roster` and `accounts` for identity-roster policies, `changes` and `deployments` for change-management policies.
- Manual evidence goes in `{prefix}{evidence_catalog_id}/{period_id}/` of the `manual.pdf` storage (default prefix `manual/`), where `{period_id}` is the entry's own cadence window (annual `2026`, quarterly `2026-Q1`). `sigcomply evidence due --all` prints every folder.
- One repository holds one framework, one config and one evidence vault.
- The CLI is source-available under the Elastic License 2.0, not open source. It is free to use; the paid part is SigComply Cloud. Releases up to v0.90.1 were Apache-2.0.

## Tutorials

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): First local check against one AWS account, into a local vault.
- [Run SigComply in CI](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): Bucket vault, CI workflows, AWS OIDC, optional cloud submission, manual evidence upload.

## How-to guides

- [Install](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/install.md): Install the CLI, pin a version, verify.
- [Configure sources](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/configure-sources.md): Add providers with read-only credentials.
- [Identity roster](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/identity-roster.md): Check every system's accounts against the directory that lists your people.
- [CI on GitHub](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/ci-github.md): Scaffolded GitHub Actions workflows and AWS OIDC.
- [CI on GitLab](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/ci-gitlab.md): Scaffolded `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pipeline schedules and AWS OIDC.
- [Manual evidence](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/manual-evidence.md): Upload documents and build declaration PDFs.
- [Vendor and third-party risk](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/vendor-risk.md): Collect assurance documents per vendor.
- [ISMS clauses and the SoA](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/isms-clauses.md): ISO 27001 clause 4-10 requirements and the Statement of Applicability.
- [Cloud dashboard](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/cloud-dashboard.md): Connect a repository to SigComply Cloud.
- [Verify evidence](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/verify-evidence.md): Check signatures and coverage with `sigcomply report`.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): Common errors.

## Reference

- [Commands](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/reference/commands.md): Commands, flags, exit codes.
- [Configuration](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/configuration.md): Every `.sigcomply.yaml` key and environment variable.
- [Sources](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/reference/sources.md): Per-source keys, credentials and permissions.
- [Frameworks](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/reference/frameworks.md): Framework IDs and counts.

- [For AI agents](https://github.com/SigComply/sigcomply-cli/blob/main/docs/for-ai-agents.md): Setup runbook and an `AGENTS.md` template.
